chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Abū Kahmas, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgot and performed eight circuits of tawaf.

He said: If he remembers before reaching the Corner, then let him stop, and it has sufficed for him. But if he does not remember until he reaches it, then let him complete fourteen circuits and perform four rakʿahs.

So this does not contradict the earlier report that we presented from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from his statement: Whoever performs tawaf of the House and mistakenly continues until entering the eighth, then let him complete fourteen circuits. That report is general, while this report is detailed, and ruling by the detailed report takes precedence over the general one, as has already been explained.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: it was sufficient and legally valid
key_terms.أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ: four units of salat (prayer) to be performed
key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ شَوْطًا: fourteen total circuits to be completed in this circumstance
key_terms.الرُّكْنَ: the Corner of the Kaʿbah referred to in the tawaf route

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone accidentally performs eight circuits in tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who mistakenly performs eight circuits in tawaf. It distinguishes between remembering before reaching the Corner and after reaching it, and it also shows a juristic method of preferring the more detailed report over a more general one.
